skill.name: starknet-wallet
skill.description: Guide Starknet wallet operations for AI agents, including balances, transfers, contract calls, paymasters, session keys, and account abstraction.
skill.summary: Guide guarded Starknet wallet queries and state-changing operations for AI agents.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, TypeScript templates, public configuration variables, and a fixed relative import. Confirmed risks involve wallet credentials and documented state-changing transaction capabilities. No shell execution, credential exfiltration, prompt injection, or user-controlled path traversal was found.

remediation.issue: The agent runtime receives a wallet signing private key.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated low-value wallet or external signer. Never expose an owner key, and restrict secret access to transaction code.

remediation.issue: Transfers and arbitrary contract invocations can change asset ownership or allowances.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, simulation, address allowlists, spending limits, expiry, and revocation before any state-changing operation.

remediation.issue: The setup places signing credentials in a plaintext environment file.
remediation.suggestion: Use a secret manager, exclude environment files from source control, restrict file permissions, and rotate any exposed key immediately.

remediation.issue: Examples depend on external RPC, token metadata, and paymaster services.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist endpoints, verify chain identifiers, pin trusted providers, and avoid sending transactions through untrusted infrastructure.

content.value_statement: Starknet wallet workflows require careful handling of balances, transactions, contracts, and signing credentials. This skill provides practical guidance and guarded examples for these operations.
actual_capabilities: Check one ERC-20 token balance through Starknet RPC.
Query multiple token balances through BalanceChecker with RPC fallback.
Prepare token transfers with optional paymaster gas payments.
Read and invoke contract entrypoints, including multicalls.
Resolve token symbols and metadata through AVNU services.
Explain constrained session-key policies for agent transactions.
limitations: State changes require a user-provided RPC endpoint, account address, and signing credential.
The package does not bundle the referenced Starknet MCP server tools.
Included scripts query balances; transfer and contract operations are documentation examples.
Fees, token metadata, and paymaster availability depend on external services.

use_cases.title: Build an agent wallet workflow
use_cases.description: Design guarded balance checks, transfers, and contract calls for a Starknet application.

use_cases.title: Monitor wallet balances
use_cases.description: Query one or many token balances and choose an efficient RPC strategy.

use_cases.title: Define session-key controls
use_cases.description: Plan contract allowlists, spending limits, expiry, and revocation for constrained agent autonomy.

prompt_templates.title: Check one token balance
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the {token} balance for {wallet_address} on {network}. Use read-only operations and explain the required configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Compare portfolio balances
prompt_templates.prompt: Check balances for {token_list} at {wallet_address}. Prefer one batch query, and explain any fallback method.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a guarded transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare, but do not submit, a transfer of {amount} {token} to {recipient}. Estimate fees and request explicit confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Design constrained agent authority
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a session-key policy for {workflow}. Include contract allowlists, methods, spending limits, expiry, simulation, confirmation, and revocation.

output_examples.input: Check the ETH balance for a Starknet wallet.
output_examples.output: The wallet holds 1.5000 ETH. The result includes the wallet address, token address, raw amount, and decimals.

output_examples.input: Review ETH, STRK, USDC, and USDT balances.
output: A batch RPC fallback remains available.

output_examples.output: The transfer plan lists the recipient, amount, token, fee method, and estimated fee. Submission waits for explicit confirmation.

best_practices: Use read-only queries before preparing any transaction.
Keep signing keys outside general agent context and use low-value accounts.
Simulate transactions and verify network, recipient, token, amount, and fees before confirmation.
anti_patterns: Do not expose an owner wallet private key to the agent runtime.
Do not submit transfers or contract writes without explicit confirmation.
Do not trust arbitrary RPC, token metadata, paymaster, or contract addresses.

faq.question: Does this skill create or deploy a wallet?
faq.answer: It explains wallet setup and operations. The included scripts do not create or deploy accounts.

faq.question: Can it move funds automatically?
faq.answer: The documentation covers state-changing operations. Production workflows should require confirmation and enforce policy limits.

faq.question: Which tokens are supported?
faq.answer: Examples cover ETH, STRK, USDC, and USDT. Other tokens can use verified symbols or contract addresses.

faq.question: Are gasless transactions supported?
faq.answer: The documentation shows AVNU paymaster usage and token-based gas payment. Availability depends on network and provider support.

faq.question: How should signing keys be stored?
faq.answer: Prefer an external signer or secret manager. Use a dedicated low-value account and never expose an owner key.

faq.question: Is the Starknet MCP server included?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents MCP tool usage, while this package includes balance-query scripts and examples.
